html:
In the app

File → New Project… → A graded level → 7. Guided mode opens on this chapter: the tags, every rung below under its fold, a Verify check, and six results: the camera inspects a bottle, a result is acknowledged, a defective bottle is rejected, the level completes, every bottle in the right bin, under par.

This level is the one most plants would recognise first: a camera on the line. Finished bottles arrive from an upstream line, filled, capped and labeled, but about a third of them have one defect: no cap, no label, or a short fill. An In-Sight smart camera on a stand over the belt looks at each bottle as it passes. Your program triggers it, takes each result, carries it down the belt to the reject pusher, and pushes every defective bottle into Reject_Bin. The good ones run on into Good_Bin at the end of the belt. Twenty bottles, par 45 s.

The camera is not a made-up part. It is a camera module in I/O Configuration, Cam1, built from Cognex’s own device file for the In-Sight 5700 series, at 192.168.1.18. Every tag is named the way the real camera names it, so the rungs in this chapter are the rungs you would write for a real 5705 on a CompactLogix. The camera’s job here is Bottle inspection: three tools, one for the cap, one for the label, one for the fill level.

The machine

The camera’s tags

The module’s tags are Cam1:O.… (the PLC writes them) and Cam1:I.… (the camera writes them). The ones this level uses:

TagMeaning
Cam1:O.Trigger_EnableAllows triggers at all. Off, the camera ignores Trigger and Trigger_Ready stays off.
Cam1:O.TriggerRising edge: acquire an image now.
TagMeaning
Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_EnableQueue results until each one is acknowledged (below).
Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_AckThe PLC has read the result.
Cam1:I.Trigger_ReadyThe camera can take a trigger: on line, enabled, not acquiring or inspecting.
Cam1:I.Trigger_AckThe trigger was taken; stays on until Trigger goes off.
Cam1:I.Missed_AcqA trigger arrived while the camera was busy: that bottle has no image.
Cam1:I.System_BusyAcquiring or inspecting.
Cam1:I.Inspection_CompletedChanges state at the end of every inspection: it toggles, so look for a change, not for a 1.
Cam1:I.Results_ValidA result is presented in the tags below.
Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_OverrunA result was thrown away because the buffer was full.
Cam1:I.Job_PassThe presented result passed.
Cam1:I.Inspection_IDThe number of the inspection the presented result belongs to.
Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_CodeBit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill, bit 3 no part in view; 0 is a good bottle.
Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[…]The result data: bytes 0-3 the part’s serial number, 4-5 the result code, 6 the size (1 S, 2 M, 3 L), 7 metal, 8 pass, 9 the fill in % of the label.

The two handshakes

The trigger. Wait for Trigger_Ready, raise Trigger, wait for Trigger_Ack, drop Trigger; the camera drops Trigger_Ack. System_Busy covers the 30 ms exposure and the 150 ms inspection, and Trigger_Ready comes back when both are over. Trigger while it is busy and nothing is acquired: Missed_Acq comes on and that bottle goes by with no image.

The result. When an inspection ends, the camera presents its result and raises Results_Valid. Read the result, then raise Inspection_Results_Ack. The camera drops Results_Valid, and then the PLC drops the ack. That makes four edges, always in that order: Valid up, Ack up, Valid down, Ack down.

Buffered results. With Buffer_Results_Enable on, a result that finishes while the last one is still unacknowledged is not thrown away. It waits in a queue, up to the camera’s buffer depth (4 here), and the camera presents it once the PLC has finished the handshake for the one before. With buffering off, each new result simply overwrites the last, whether the PLC has read it or not. Buffering is what lets the program look away for a scan or two without losing a bottle. It has a limit, though: a result that finds the queue full is lost, and Results_Buffer_Overrun comes on. Lose one result and every bottle after it gets the wrong verdict, because the FIFO is one short.

How the level is scored

What happensPoints
A defective bottle in Reject_Bin+100
A good bottle in Good_Bin+100
A defective bottle in Good_Bin (shipped)−100
A good bottle in Reject_Bin−50
A bottle that passes the camera without being inspected−25
Complete under par+200

How to pass it, step by step

1. Set the camera up once. Trigger_Enable and Buffer_Results_Enable on whenever the

2. Space the bottles. A timer that restarts itself releases one every 0.9 s. At 80 px/s that puts four or five

3. Trigger once per bottle. An ONS on PE_Trigger latches a request; the trigger goes out only when the

4. Take each result into a FIFO. Results_Valid and not yet acknowledged: FFL the result code into

5. Unload at the pusher. When a bottle reaches PE_Reject, FFU the oldest code. Bottles on a belt stay in

6. Light the fault lamp on anything that breaks the one-to-one match between bottles and results: an

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

TagTypeKindDescription
Start_PBBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.8Start push button, momentary
RunBOOLbase tagSeal-in run bit
Stop_PBBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.9Stop push button, momentary
E_StopBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.10E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy
Conveyor_RunBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.1Belt motor
Lamp_RunBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.3Run lamp
Infeed_ReadyBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.0Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released
Rel_TTIMERbase tagSpaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s
Infeed_ReleaseBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.0Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)
PE_TriggerBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.2Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view
Trig_ONSBOOLbase tag
Trig_ReqBOOLbase tagA bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection
Res_QDINTbase tagThe result codes of the inspected bottles between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first
Res_Q_CtlCONTROLbase tagFIFO control for Res_Q
PE_RejectBOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.5Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher
Rej_ONSBOOLbase tag
CurDINTbase tagThe result code of the bottle at the reject pusher
Rej_ONS2BOOLbase tag
FireBOOLbase tagArmed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected
RejectBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.2Reject pusher cylinder
Cnt_ONSBOOLbase tag
Reject_CountDINTbase tagShown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected
Pass_CountDINTbase tagShown on the toolbar: bottles you let through
Lamp_FaultBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.4Fault lamp

Run, setup and release

Rung 2 has no Run in it on purpose. Rung 3 is the self-restarting timer of chapter 7: XIO(Rel_T.DN) resets it the scan after it is done, so Rel_T.DN is on for exactly one scan, which rung 4 turns into one rising edge on Infeed_Release.

The trigger handshake

The request is latched because the eye’s edge and the camera being ready do not have to happen in the same scan. With 0.9 s between bottles and 180 ms of camera time they always do here, but the program does not rely on it. Rung 7 drops Trigger the moment the camera acknowledges it; a Trigger held on is not a second trigger, and the camera waits for it to drop before it can be acknowledged again.

The results handshake

FFL loads on the rung going true. Latching the ack on the same rung makes the rung go false on the next scan, so each result is loaded exactly once, even though Results_Valid stays on until the camera sees the ack. Rung 9 is the other half: the ack comes off when Valid has gone, and only then does the camera present the next queued result.

The reject pusher and the counts

The pattern is Level 5’s diverter, with one FIFO instead of one per zone: unload on the eye’s rising edge, arm, push while the bottle is at the eye, disarm when it has gone. The counts are for the toolbar; the score card keeps the official ones.

The fault lamp

Run it

Load your program, Run mode, Start. Camera_HMI shows each image as it is taken, with the three tools drawn on it in green or red. In a run on v2.02, 20 of 20 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 38 s against a par of 45 s: 2200 points and three stars.

Watch for: the toggle and the level

Inspection_Completed toggles. A rung with XIC(Cam1:I.Inspection_Completed) on it is true for every other inspection, not every one. If you want to use it, remember its last state in a BOOL and compare. Results_Valid with the ack handshake is simpler, and it is the signal that means the result is ready to read.

Watch for: acking without dropping

Raise the ack and never drop it (leave out rung 9) and you get exactly one result. With buffering on, the camera queues the next four and throws the fifth away, and from then on every verdict belongs to a different bottle. The fault lamp lights on the overrun, but by then the FIFO is already wrong.

Try it: see an overrun

Take rung 9 out and run. Watch the RESULT BUFFER bar on Camera_HMI climb to 4 / 4 and the overrun count start. Then put rung 9 back, take out Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable in rung 2, and slow the ack by putting TON(Ack_T,500,0) before it: the results overwrite each other instead, and nothing tells you, which is why plants buffer.

Try it: a missed acquisition

Set Rel_T to 300 ms and take XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready) out of rung 6. Some bottles now arrive while the camera is still inspecting the last: Missed_Acq, the fault lamp, and −25 for every bottle that passes uninspected.

On a real camera

The module’s Mode in I/O Configuration is Simulated, and the Vision Sensor then plays the camera. In the desktop app, switch Cam1 to implicit I/O at the camera’s address and the same program drives a real In-Sight. The real camera takes the trigger, runs its own job on whatever is under its lens, and sends back its own Job_Pass, result code and Results_Valid. The sim only mirrors its bits: the ring light flashes when the real camera acquires. That mode is for working the handshake on real hardware and is not scored, because the score is kept against the sim’s bottles. For the program to work unchanged, the job on the camera has to report the same result layout: the defect bits in the result code and the fill in the result data. Which spreadsheet cells feed those is set in In-Sight Explorer’s EtherNet/IP settings.

Card mode: the card decides

On a live camera the verdict comes from whatever is under the lens, and the sim’s bottles have their own defects, so the two do not match and the run is not scored. Card mode fixes that. Tick Card mode in the Camera’s properties and the hopper sends only good bottles; each bottle waits at the camera until its result is presented, then takes that verdict and moves on. The verdict comes from a bottle card under the camera:

CardBottleResult codeFill (byte 9)Card ID (byte 10)
SN-4801good01001
SN-4802no cap11002
SN-4803no label21003
SN-4804short fill4704
no cardno part in view: a reject800

Level 7’s rungs do not change: they trigger, read the code, carry it in the FIFO and reject on it, exactly as before. What changes is the belt. A bottle that waits at the camera holds the bottles behind it, so the line runs at the pace of the camera’s answers, and with a real camera that is the pace at which you swap cards.

With the simulated camera, choose the card in Card under the lens, or on Camera_HMI’s CARDS page touch the card you want under the lens. The page draws the four cards as the camera sees them through the red filter and keeps a tally per card: what it should read, how many times it was seen, how many it read right and its last code. MAIN names the card on the image, reads HOLDING while a bottle waits for its result, and turns the card line red when a card reads the wrong verdict.

With a real camera (Cam1 on implicit I/O in the desktop app), the 5705 decides. The sim reads three things from it when Results_Valid rises: Inspection_Result_Code for the verdict, byte 9 of Inspection_Results for the fill and byte 10 for the card ID. The job on the camera writes those, so the card ID is something the job reads off the card, not something typed in. A result whose code does not match its card ID shows up on the CARDS page and in the event log.

Try it: swap cards mid-run

Tick Card mode, start with SN-4801 under the lens and run. After five bottles touch SN-4804 on the CARDS page, then the empty card, then SN-4803. Watch each bottle stop under the camera, take the card, and go to the bin its verdict sends it to. The score card at the end lists every card you used, and if the rungs are right every count in the Right column matches Seen.

Try it: break the ack

In card mode, take rung 9 out (the ack never drops). The first bottle gets its verdict, the second waits at the camera and never moves: its result is in the buffer but never presented, and the line stays held. Put the rung back and the line runs again. That is the same fault as the overrun Try it, made visible on the belt.

The bottle cards

The cards are printed on the bench printer from STEP files in the repository’s cards folder: 100 × 70 × 4 mm, a chamfered corner so a card only sits one way in its nest, and two bodies in each file, a dark base and red features inlaid 0.8 mm and standing 0.6 mm proud. Through the red band-pass filter the red reads bright and the base dark. Everything on a card is something the job uses: the bottle’s outline (to locate it), the cap, the liquid (its top edge is the fill line), a label window with the product name for OCR, and a DataMatrix that encodes the card’s number. There is no text for people on a card.

The number is SN-48RK: R is the product (0 SODA, 1 WATER, 2 MILK, 3 JUICE, 4 OIL) and K the defect (1 good, 2 no cap, 3 no label, 4 short fill at 70 %). The job puts R × 10 + K in byte 10, so the SODA set reads 1 to 4, the IDs in the table above. Level 7 uses the SODA set; Level 12 uses the whole set (see its chapter, Card mode on Level 12). On Camera_HMI’s CARDS page a tab per product picks the row of four cards.

The camera’s own image

With Cam1 live, the camera screen shows the picture the 5705 actually took. Every time Inspection_Complete toggles, the page asks the bridge for it; the bridge logs in to the camera’s FTP server, reads image.bmp (an In-Sight always keeps its last acquired image there), scales it down to the width set in the Camera’s properties and hands it back. The screen fits it into the image pane and writes under it what came back from the camera: the result code, the fill (byte 9) and the card (byte 10). The camera’s own graphics are not in image.bmp; it is the raw image.

Nothing is added to the camera job for this. The bridge pulls the file, so there are no spreadsheet cells, no Event and no FTP server on the PC. The login is admin with a blank password unless you set another user (one with FTP Read under Sensor → User Access Settings) in the Camera’s properties: Live image, FTP user, FTP password and width to fetch. One fetch runs at a time; inspections that finish while an image is on its way ask for one more when it lands, so at a fast trigger rate the screen shows the latest image, not every one. A refused login or a camera that does not answer is written in the pane. Touch the image and it fills the screen: the IMAGE view shows it as large as Camera_HMI allows, with the inspection ID, the image size and how long the fetch took above it, and the code, fill and card below. Touch it again to go back. Live image: width to fetch sets the size the bridge sends: 800 is plenty for the screen; set it to the camera’s own width (1600 on a 5603) to get every pixel on the screen. FULL SIZE on the IMAGE view goes further: it fetches the last image unscaled and opens it over the whole window, with Fit, 100, 200 and 400 %, scrolling to pan, and the pixel under the pointer with its grey value, which is handy for checking a threshold or a DataMatrix module against what the job sees. Esc closes it. The screen keeps its smaller copy, so the full image is only fetched when you ask for it.

Each image is work for the camera, on top of inspecting and keeping the I/O connection going, so Live image: at most one image every (1 s by default) keeps a fast trigger from queueing one fetch after another. If a busy camera goes quiet for a moment, the I/O connection is held, not dropped: the module log says stalled and then resumed after the stall, and only ten seconds of silence closes and reopens it. On an older camera such as the 5603, an RPI of 50–100 ms and In-Sight Explorer offline (no live video) keep the stalls away.

A real In-Sight 4.x job

On In-Sight 4.x firmware (a 5603, say) a spreadsheet job sends its results to the PLC with two cells: FormatOutputBuffer, which packs values into bytes, and WriteEIPBuffer(A0, …), which puts them in Inspection_Results after each inspection. Lay them out the way the simulated camera does, and Logix Connect reads them where it expects them:

BytesValueFormat
0–3inspection count32-bit
4–5result code (bit 0 no cap, 1 no label, 2 short fill, 3 no card, 4 wrong product)16-bit
6, 708-bit
8pass (1/0)8-bit
9fill %8-bit
10card ID, R × 10 + K8-bit

Then set the Camera’s Live camera: where the inspection ID and result code are read to Results buffer: the screen, the RESULTS page and card mode take the ID from bytes 0–3 and the code from bytes 4–5. On 4.x the module’s own Inspection_Result_Code field is not set by the job, so Level 7’s results rung has to read the code from the buffer too: FFL(Cam1:I.Inspection_Results[4],Res_Q[0],Res_Q_Ctl,8) in place of the code field, the change you would make on a real line with that camera. Two more things a 4.x camera does its own way. With Buffer_Results_Enable on, it raises Results_Valid only when the job writes a results buffer; a job without WriteEIPBuffer never raises it, Level 7’s results rung never runs, and nothing is rejected. (The screen still counts such a camera’s inspections on Inspection_Complete until it has seen Results_Valid once.) And PASS / FAIL on the screen is the camera’s Job_Pass, which follows the job’s pass/fail cell (Sensor → Job Pass/Fail Cell Setup): a cell such as And($F$6==1,$F$13==1) that is 1 when the label read and the code decoded.

Try it: sn-4801 to sn-4804 on a real camera

With the two buffer cells in the job and Results buffer selected, put each SODA card under the lens in turn and trigger. SN-4801 should read code 0, fill 100 and card 1; SN-4802 code 1 (no cap); SN-4803 code 2 (no label: the OCR fails); SN-4804 code 4 with fill 70 and card 4. The CARDS page tallies every one, and any card whose code does not match what it should read shows red: that is the job to fix, not the program.

Without card mode, a live camera’s inspections count too. Each time Inspection_Complete toggles (or Results_Valid rises, with the results buffer on) the screen takes the camera’s Inspection_ID, its result code, Job_Pass and, on a bottle job, bytes 9 and 10, and shows them as the simulated camera’s would: PASS or FAIL, the counts, the RESULTS page and the banner. Those results do not move the sim’s bottles; that is what card mode is for.

Try it: see what the camera saw

With Cam1 live in the desktop app, tick Card mode and run Level 7 with SN-4804 under the lens. Each bottle that stops at the camera brings the card’s picture to Camera_HMI with code 4 · fill 70 % under it. Now cover half the card with your hand and trigger again: the picture shows your hand and the code shows what the job made of it. Then set FTP password to anything and watch the pane report the camera’s refusal.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in. Stop_PB is a plain button here; E_Stop is 1 while healthy

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Seal-in run bit) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The belt and the run lamp follow Run. The belt never stops for the camera: it images a moving bottle
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: CAMERA SETUP: triggering enabled and results buffered for as long as the machine is healthy. Buffered, the camera queues each result until the PLC acknowledges the one before it, so no result is overwritten while the program is busy elsewhere. Not tied to Run: a stop must not throw away the results of the bottles still on the belt

pred.q: E_Stop is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable is off and Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable is off. It stops at XIC(E_Stop).

rungs.words: When E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Trigger_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable) Output Energize does: turns Cam1:O.Buffer_Results_Enable on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: RELEASE: a timer that restarts itself, so a bottle every 0.9 s while the hopper exit is clear. The bottles arrive at the camera 72 px apart, four or five of them between the camera and the reject pusher
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and Rel_T.DN (the done bit of Rel_T: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) is off, the rung runs the timer Rel_T (Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) toward 900 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  3. XIO(Rel_T.DN) Examine If Open asks: true when Rel_T.DN is off.
  4. TON(Rel_T,900,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Rel_T toward 900 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Rel_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: One scan of Infeed_Release is one rising edge: one bottle

pred.q: Rel_T.DN is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Infeed_Release is on.

rungs.words: When Rel_T.DN (the done bit of Rel_T: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s) is on, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Rel_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rel_T.DN is on.
  2. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: A BOTTLE AT THE CAMERA: the eye sees it arrive; remember that it wants an inspection
rungs.words: When PE_Trigger (Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung latches Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Trigger) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Trigger is on.
  2. ONS(Trig_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Trig_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. OTL(Trig_Req) Output Latch does: latches Trig_Req on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Trig_Req stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: TRIGGER only when the camera says it can take one (Trigger_Ready); a trigger while it is busy would be a missed acquisition

pred.q: Trig_Req is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Cam1:O.Trigger is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready).

rungs.words: When Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection) is on and Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on, the rung latches Cam1:O.Trigger on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trig_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trig_Req is on.
  2. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ready is on.
  3. OTL(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Trigger on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Trigger stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: The camera has taken the trigger (Trigger_Ack): drop Trigger, ready for the next bottle. Trigger_Ack stays on until Trigger goes off
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger and unlatches Trig_Req (A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Trigger_Ack is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Cam1:O.Trigger) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Trigger. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Trig_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Trig_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Trigger when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: A RESULT: load its code into the FIFO (0 = pass; bit 0 no cap, bit 1 no label, bit 2 short fill) and acknowledge it in the same scan. With the ack on, the rung goes false, so the FFL loads exactly once
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on and Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off, the rung loads Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into the queue Res_Q[0] (The result codes of the inspected bottles between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first) and latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is on.
  2. XIO(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. FFL(Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code,Res_Q[0],Res_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Load does: loads Cam1:I.Inspection_Result_Code into the queue Res_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Latch does: latches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.
pats.think: a ticket roll at a deli counter: the first ticket torn off is the first one served.
pats.watch: A load and an unload must happen once per part each. A part that leaves the line between the two (a reject, a part picked off) has to be unloaded too, or every answer after it belongs to the wrong part.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: The camera has dropped Results_Valid: drop the ack. Only now does it present the next buffered result: the handshake is four edges, Valid up, Ack up, Valid down, Ack down
rungs.words: When Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off, the rung unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Cam1:I.Results_Valid) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Valid is off.
  2. OTU(Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Cam1:O.Inspection_Results_Ack when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: AT THE REJECT PUSHER: a bottle arrives at its eye; the oldest result in the FIFO is that bottle's, because bottles on a belt stay in order
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung unloads the oldest entry of Res_Q[0] (The result codes of the inspected bottles between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first) into Cur (The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. FFU(Res_Q[0],Cur,Res_Q_Ctl,8) FIFO Unload does: unloads the oldest entry of Res_Q[0] into Cur. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: Any defect bit set: arm the pusher
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on, this is the first scan of it and Cur (The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher) is not 0, the rung latches Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS2) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS2). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. NEQ(Cur,0) Not Equal asks: true when Cur is not 0.
  4. OTL(Fire) Output Latch does: latches Fire on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Fire stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: Push while the bottle is at the eye

pred.q: PE_Reject is on and Fire is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Reject is on.

rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) is on, the rung turns Reject (Reject pusher cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
  3. OTE(Reject) Output Energize does: turns Reject on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: if Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) is on, it makes Reject_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected) = Reject_Count + 1; if Fire is off, it makes Pass_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles you let through) = Pass_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Cnt_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Cnt_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
    2. ADD(Reject_Count,1,Reject_Count) Add does: makes Reject_Count = Reject_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Fire) Examine If Open asks: true when Fire is off.
    2. ADD(Pass_Count,1,Pass_Count) Add does: makes Pass_Count = Pass_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 14

pred.q: PE_Reject is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fire is left as it was. It stops at XIO(PE_Reject).

rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is off, the rung unlatches Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Reject) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Reject is off.
  2. OTU(Fire) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fire. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fire when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: FAULT LAMP: a result lost to a full buffer, a trigger the camera missed, or the camera off line. Any of these and the FIFO no longer matches the bottles
rungs.words: When either (Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on), (Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on) or (Cam1:I.Online is off), the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Results_Buffer_Overrun is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Cam1:I.Missed_Acq) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cam1:I.Missed_Acq is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIO(Cam1:I.Online) Examine If Open asks: true when Cam1:I.Online is off.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Infeed_Ready.desc: Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released

Rel_T.desc: Spaces the releases: one bottle every 0.9 s

Infeed_Release.desc: Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)

PE_Trigger.desc: Presence eye at the camera: a bottle is in the field of view

Trig_Req.desc: A bottle has reached PE_Trigger and wants an inspection

Res_Q.desc: The result codes of the inspected bottles between the camera and the reject pusher, oldest first

PE_Reject.desc: Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher

Cur.desc: The result code of the bottle at the reject pusher

Fire.desc: Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected

Reject_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles you rejected

Pass_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles you let through
